title: Night at the Museum
statementMd:
Grigoriy, like the hero of one famous comedy film, found a job as a night security guard at the museum. At first night he received *embosser* and was to take stock of the whole exposition.

*Embosser* is a special devise that allows to "print" the text of a plastic tape. Text is printed sequentially, character by character. The device consists of a wheel with a lowercase English letters written in a circle, static pointer to the current letter and a button that print the chosen letter. At one move it's allowed to rotate the alphabetic wheel one step clockwise or counterclockwise. Initially, static pointer points to letter '`a`'. Other letters are located as shown on the picture:

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f9a6625d44375aa879555a962abab58252e0f103.png)

After Grigoriy add new item to the base he has to print its name on the plastic tape and attach it to the corresponding exhibit. It's not required to return the wheel to its initial position with pointer on the letter '`a`'.

Our hero is afraid that some exhibits may become alive and start to attack him, so he wants to print the names as fast as possible. Help him, for the given string find the minimum number of rotations of the wheel required to print it.

## Input

The only line of input contains the name of some exhibit — the non-empty string consisting of no more than $100$ characters. It's guaranteed that the string consists of only lowercase English letters.

## Output

Print one integer — the minimum number of rotations of the wheel, required to print the name given in the input.

## Note

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7a9f692be97294f6f0dedd91b5e5794fcea7c621.png)

To print the string from the first sample it would be optimal to perform the following sequence of rotations:

1. from '`a`' to '`z`' ($1$ rotation counterclockwise),
2. from '`z`' to '`e`' ($5$ clockwise rotations),
3. from '`e`' to '`u`' ($10$ rotations counterclockwise),
4. from '`u`' to '`s`' ($2$ counterclockwise rotations).

In total,

1 + 5 + 10 + 2 = 18

rotations are required.
statementZhMd:
格里戈里就像某部著名喜剧电影中的主人公一样，在博物馆找到了一份夜间保安的工作。第一天晚上，他收到了一台*压印器*，需要清点整个展览。

*压印器*是一种可以在塑料带上“打印”文字的特殊设备。文字会逐个字符依次打印。该设备由一个环形排列着小写英文字母的转轮、指向当前字母的固定指针，以及一个用于打印所选字母的按钮组成。每次操作可以使字母转轮顺时针或逆时针旋转一格。初始时，固定指针指向字母“`a`”。其他字母的位置如图所示：

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f9a6625d44375aa879555a962abab58252e0f103.png)

格里戈里将新物品添加到记录后，必须把它的名称打印在塑料带上，并将其贴到对应的展品上。不要求在打印结束后将指针转回字母“`a`”。

我们的主人公担心某些展品可能会活过来并开始攻击他，因此他希望尽可能快地打印出这些名称。请你帮助他：对于给定的字符串，求打印它所需的最少转轮旋转次数。

## 输入格式

输入仅一行，包含某个展品的名称——一个非空字符串，长度不超过 $100$ 个字符。保证该字符串只由小写英文字母组成。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——打印输入中给定名称所需的最少转轮旋转次数。

## 说明

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7a9f692be97294f6f0dedd91b5e5794fcea7c621.png)

打印第一个样例中的字符串时，最优的旋转过程如下：

1. 从“`a`”转到“`z`”（逆时针旋转 $1$ 次）；
2. 从“`z`”转到“`e`”（顺时针旋转 $5$ 次）；
3. 从“`e`”转到“`u`”（逆时针旋转 $10$ 次）；
4. 从“`u`”转到“`s`”（逆时针旋转 $2$ 次）。

总计需要

1 + 5 + 10 + 2 = 18

次旋转。
